Author of multiple books on church leadership and organizational growth
biography.education: B.A., Jarvis Christian College, Hawkins, TX; M.Div., Gammon Theological Seminary, Interdenominational Theological Center, Atlanta, GA
biography.background: Brown founded Impact Church in 2007 from a core team of 25 people and grew it to 5,000+ in-person and online weekly attendees with a $4M operating budget. He retired from pastoral ministry in June 2022 and now runs a coaching and consulting firm, Culverhouse, LLC, serving business and church leaders. He is the only candidate in the 2026 Democratic field with no prior electoral office. Born in Lufkin, TX; has lived in Atlanta/Georgia area for nearly 30 years. Father of four.

lgbtqInclusion.quote: If you're going to fight for Black Lives Matter and say that you got to get your foot off my neck, and then in the next breath you tell your own brother and sister that they can't get married because they're in a same-sex relationship — that's an injustice
lgbtqInclusion.notes: Brown explicitly framed LGBTQ+ inclusion as a social justice issue during his pastoral tenure, placing it alongside racial justice. He described an evolution of his views after a regrettable anti-same-sex-relationship sermon led to a transformative conversation with an affected parishioner. Also stated: 'the isms have the same tactics, whether it's sexism, racism, classism, they all use the same tactics of oppression, but we hide it in theology and the Bible.' This is a significant pre-campaign position signal on civil rights/LGBTQ+ issues, unusual for a Black megachurch pastor.

socialJusticeMinistry.notes: Impact Church's stated mission included bringing 'healing, justice and compassion to the world.' Brown described his church as 'inclusive' and 'compelled to help bring healing, justice and compassion.' This background is consistent with progressive social justice orientation but predates his campaign and should be weighted accordingly.

evidenceSummary.notes: Brown is a first-time candidate in a crowded primary. His policy record is almost entirely built on forum appearances and media interviews over a ~20-month campaign. He has consistent, credible positions on healthcare access, education/teacher pay, small business economics, and general affordability. His pastoral record provides a strong LGBTQ+ justice signal that is unusual in its explicitness. However, he has not publicly addressed several major scoring axes including reproductive rights, gun policy, immigration/ICE, criminal justice, climate, or transit — likely because forums have not forced those questions or he is avoiding positional risk as a lower-tier primary candidate. The abortion gap is particularly notable given it is a defining issue in Georgia. Scorer should note that the absence of evidence is not evidence of absence but cannot be scored. Confidence levels per axis should be flagged accordingly. Among Democratic primary candidates he is consistently positioned as a progressive outsider; his strongest differentiation is the small business / rural equity framing and personal faith-to-justice arc.
